definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 defines method as 'A procedural entity defined by a method definition within, or inherited by, a class definition'; 2023 drops the entry and describes methods at §2023:9.3.4, whose text is word for word §2002:9.3.4. The rule's 'method definition' denotes the same source element in both editions, so the entries GLOBAL is forbidden in (factory, instance, method definitions) are unchanged.

pending-clause.answer: §2002:9.3.5 (Method invocation) binds an invocation by method-name up the inheritance hierarchy at runtime; 2023 renumbers it 9.3.6 and adds parametric polymorphism (signature resolution, 2023 9.3.5). The rule restricts where GLOBAL may be written and does not depend on how an invocation is bound; the 2002 refusals (COBOL1520) remain the evidence.
